title: Dashboard signal deadzone repair and forward-fill playbook
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Multiple customers across Hosted, Dedicated, and Private deployments reported dashboards showing zero or stale signal (missing metric tiles and explorer gaps) during a rolling ingestion compaction window. Symptoms: live panels returned empty arrays, tenant explorer queries returned 0 results for recent windows, and trace-to-metric links did not materialize for spans emitted during the incident. Incident surfaced via SRE Pager and two escalations from enterprise customers.
technical_root_cause: A race between snapshot eviction and the time-series forward-index compaction produced temporary index holes for tenants with high write churn. The compaction job pruned recent segment pointers when snapshot checkpointing lagged; the query layer had no robust forward-fill heuristic, so a short-lived absence of index pointers returned no data rather than attempting a backfill. Trace-to-metric stitching failed because the span index write was visible but the metric index pointers were missing for the same time bucket.
immediate_mitigation: Rolled back aggressive compaction policy for affected backend pool (decrease compaction_frequency and increase retention window)
Enabled emergency read-time forward-fill in query router for impacted tenant shards (temporary patch)
Triggered controlled rehydration job to rebuild forward index segments for affected tenants from raw ingesters (prioritized customers first)
Opened customer comms channel and posted interim status to affected tenants with ETA and mitigations
long_term_fix_plan: 1) Harden compaction checkpointing: ensure compaction never prunes segments younger than last successful snapshot commit; add monotonicity guard
2) Implement robust forward-fill semantics in query service: when pointer absence detected for recent window, attempt on-the-fly lightweight backfill from ingest logs before returning empty tiles
3) Add transactional ordering guarantees between snapshotter and compactor with explicit fence token to prevent races
4) Ship background reindex worker that can be run per-tenant during low load windows to heal residual holes
5) Add end-to-end canary tests that simulate churned tenants and verify dashboard continuity under compaction + snapshot cycles
6) Update runbook and enable alerting on 'dashboard-empty-tiles' anomaly (new SLO-backed symptom)
acceptance_criteria: Backfill worker can rehydrate 24 hours of missing index for a tenant within SLA (target 30m for small tenants, 4h for large)
Query service returns forward-filled results for transient index pointer loss with no more than 2x query latency increase
Compaction changes include automated safety checks and unit/integration tests preventing pruning younger-than-snapshot segments
Canary job demonstrates zero dashboard-empty incidents in two 24h runs under synthetic churn
Customer regression tests (two affected tenants) validate restored dashboards and trace links
steps_to_reproduce: Create a tenant with high metric ingestion rate and short metric TTL (simulate churn)
Trigger snapshotting but delay commit (introduce artificial lag in snapshotter)
Run compaction job to prune forward-index segments in the same window
Query dashboards/explorer for recent windows -> observe empty tiles if not backfilled
Emit spans alongside metrics -> observe missing trace-to-metric links until rehydration
mitigation_and_rollback: If forward-fill patch causes unacceptable latency, flip routing to legacy read path (feature flag controllable)
Rollback compaction policy change via infra orchestration if rehydration job impacts disk IO beyond thresholds
Emergency SLA: for enterprise customers, start manual reindex prioritization until automation passes canaries

postmortem_summary: Race between compaction and snapshot checkpointing caused short-lived index holes that manifested as empty dashboard tiles and missing trace-to-metric links. Emergency mitigations restored most customers within hours; residual data holes were healed by the rehydration worker. Long-term fixes include transactional fences, query forward-fill, and improved canaries. Documentation and customer-facing messaging were updated.
resolution: In-progress: emergency rollback and rehydration completed for top customers; compaction fence and forward-fill feature merged to main and currently undergoing staged rollout. Final validation pending successful canary runs scheduled 2025-02-14 to 2025-02-15.
